site_or_subject: CRU Large Energy Users connection policy for datacenters
operator: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU); EirGrid/ESB Networks
record: CRU's proposed decision CRU/202504 (18 Feb 2025) recorded datacenters at ~21% of national electricity demand in 2023 (data centre and new technology load 7.1 of 30.5 TWh), ~30% by 2030-32 (13.3 TWh in 2032), and ~50% of electricity produced in Dublin/Meath; it did not quantify network-cost impacts on consumers. site_or_subject: Meta hyperscale datacenter, Zeewolde: state land sale
record: The 166 ha Meta site (figure given in the Senate by Senator Koffeman and by NOS) included land of which the State owned 'a large part' (Council of State, 2023); NOS put the State share at about 80 ha [press]. The Eerste Kamer adopted a motion on 21 Dec 2021 (35925 XIV, H) asking the government to have the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf suspend sales of agricultural land for hyperscale datacenters. In the 22 Feb 2022 interpellation Senator Koffeman (PvdD) stated that only about 15% of residual heat could be used, and the minister said the State still held the land as a private-law party but would not undo the municipal permit. Minister De Jonge's letter of 10 June 2022 (Kamerstuk 26 643 nr. 862) transmitted TNO's assessment of the municipality's plan against the Aug 2021 sale conditions. The same day the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf wrote to Zeewolde that it could not sell the land on the current assessment. TNO found the design energy-efficient for now, with intelligent cooling and no drinking water used for cooling, but roofs, facades and surrounding land not maximally used for solar, rainwater use unclear and the residual-heat plan too undeveloped to assess. On 20 Sep 2023 the Council of State annulled the Trekkersveld IV zoning plan (ECLI:NL:RVS:2023:3550), noting that neither the municipality nor the initiator owned the land and that there was no certainty the State would sell.

region: Global (Circular Centers in North America, Europe, Asia)
site_or_subject: Microsoft cloud-hardware reuse/recycle rate and third-party assurance scope
record: Microsoft's 2025 Environmental Sustainability Report states '90.9% reuse and recycling of cloud hardware servers and components' (FY24, against a 90% by 2025 goal). The April 2025 circularity white paper defines the rate as (reuse kg + recycle kg x recycling efficiency) / total kg, cites >3.2 million components reused in FY24, and mentions no independent verification. Deloitte & Touche LLP's limited-assurance review (AT-C 210, dated 29 May 2025; FY25 review dated 9 July 2026) covers Section 1 of the Environmental Data Fact Sheet, which contains operational waste tonnages and packaging recyclability but no cloud-hardware reuse/recycle percentage.

2026 Microsoft Environmental Data Fact Sheet (incl. Deloitte review report)

claim: Microsoft reports 90.9% reuse and recycling of cloud hardware servers and components in FY24, exceeding its 2025 target a year early.
gap: The 90.9% hardware circularity figure is self-reported; the named third-party review scope covers waste tonnages but does not list the hardware reuse/recycle rate.

site_or_subject: Facebook content moderators v Meta, Sama and Majorel: Court of Appeal [2024] KECA 1152
operator: Meta Platforms Inc / Meta Platforms Ireland; Samasource EPZ Ltd (Sama); Majorel Kenya Ltd
record: On 20 Sept 2024 the Court of Appeal (Musinga P, Asike-Makhandia, Mativo JJA) allowed three consolidated appeals and set aside in its entirety the ELRC's 2 June 2023 interim ruling (which had restrained the redundancy of ~184 moderators, extended contracts and ordered medical and psychological care), holding the judge 'impermissibly and dangerously delved into contested issues of fact and the law' and was 'writing a final judgment as opposed to an interlocutory ruling'. The lawfulness of the redundancy and Meta's employer status remain for trial; Meta's jurisdiction objection was not decided; each party bears its own costs.

record_sources.publisher: Kenya Law (National Council for Law Reporting)

claim: none found in the court record beyond the parties' pleadings (Meta contends it is not the moderators' employer; moderators allege sham redundancy and unsafe conditions).
gap: Interim protections were vacated on procedural grounds; the substantive labor-condition allegations are undecided as of this record.

site_or_subject: PT Indonesia Tsingshan Stainless Steel furnace explosion, 24 Dec 2023 (nickel supply chain)
operator: PT ITSS, tenant of Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park
record: IMIP's spokesperson initially reported 18 deaths (10 Indonesian, 8 Chinese) and 41 injured after a furnace explosion during repair work on 24 Dec 2023, after police revised an early toll from 13 to 18. The Indonesian National Police (Central Sulawesi Regional Police, published 4 Jan 2024) recorded 21 worker deaths and said the case had been upgraded to a formal (pro justitia) investigation into suspected violations of standard operating procedures at PT ITSS. A Tempo commentary also gives 21 deaths and reports Ministry of Manpower investigators had difficulty accessing the park. No Kemnaker, ILO or Komnas HAM inspection report with findings was retrieved.

claim: IMIP stated the blast occurred during furnace repair and attributed the initial release to slag residue contacting flammable material and oxygen tanks.

claim_sources.title: As death toll rises, Morowali blast brings work safety squarely into focus

gap: The death toll rose from the company's initial 18 to 21 in the police record; police treat the case as a criminal investigation into suspected SOP violations, but no Kemnaker, ILO or Komnas HAM inspection findings are public. Older source (2023-24).
verification_note: Fetched Indonesian National Police article (inp.polri.go.id, 4 Jan 2024): records 21 deaths and an upgraded investigation for suspected SOP violations; resolves the earlier 18-vs-21 discrepancy (18 was IMIP's initial count, per Jakarta Post) in favour of the police figure. The police item gives no nationality split or injury count, so those remain IMIP figures via the Jakarta Post; Kemnaker and Komnas HAM findings were searched for (Indonesian) and not located.
